subject: Exhibit reorder + scope rebalance (proposed change order)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: contracts@aihealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit reorder + scope rebalance (proposed change order)

Hi Jane / AI Health contracting team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, AI Health's onboarding timeline requires reordering Exhibit B so that the real-time ingestion work (SOW item 1.2) is prioritized ahead of the batch export item. To support that sequencing we propose a change order that: 

- Reorders Exhibit B so Line Item 1.2 becomes the implementation priority (no change to total committed GPU units)
- Splits the original SOW into SOW-A (implementation & ramp) and SOW-B (optimization & recurring ops) for clearer acceptance criteria and milestone billing
- Applies a one-time scope rebalance credit of $18,000 to offset the front-loaded implementation effort (applied to Month 1 invoice)

Attached is a redline of Exhibit B showing the reorder and the split into SOW-A/B (AIHealth_ExhibitB_reorder_redline_v1.pdf). Key asks from our side: 

1) Confirm that you can sign the change order on the proposed terms (redline attached) or provide line-by-line comments by COB Friday.
2) If you prefer a single consolidated change order with DocuSign, say so and we will prepare the DocuSign envelope.
3) Grace — please confirm we can apply the one-time credit against Month 1 invoice and whether we need a separate PO line.

Next steps if agreeable: Redwood legal + AI Health legal align on wording, finalize redline, then routing to procurement for PO and DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if that helps.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: AIHealth_ExhibitB_reorder_redline_v1.pdf (redline PDF, 1 page summary + markup)
From: contracts@aihealth.com <contracts@aihealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: jane.sanchez@aihealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit reorder + scope rebalance (proposed change order)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the proposed redline. Quick clarifying questions from our side before we route to procurement: 

- The $18k one-time credit — is that the only pricing concession? We want confirmation that ongoing rates and unit counts remain unchanged outside of the temporary credit.
- For SOW-A vs SOW-B: can you add explicit acceptance criteria for SOW-A milestones (post-ramp performance targets)? Our internal QA needs explicit pass/fail tests to accept implementation deliverables.
- Please provide a short mutual action plan with owners and dates so procurement can see the timeline (we need that for PO approval).

If you can add these clarifications in the redline or as a short cover note, we should be able to close this week. Otherwise, we will need one more legal pass.

Regards,

Contracts Team
AI Health
contracts@aihealth.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: contracts@aihealth.com, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit reorder + scope rebalance (proposed change order)

Hi all — looping in from legal. I reviewed the attached Exhibit B redline and added inline comments (redline_comments_markus.docx). Summary of the legal points and proposed edits: 

1) Limited-term acceptance clause: I recommend we keep acceptance criteria for SOW-A as a performance-based acceptance (30-day validation window) but remove any language that creates an open-ended warranty obligation beyond the standard MSA warranty. I've proposed alternate language in the docx.
2) Price credit mechanics: suggest we state the $18k credit as a one-time invoice-level credit applied to Invoice 1; include a short sentence that "no retroactive changes will be made to previously billed service periods."
3) Change management / future scope: added a short sentence making clear that reordering SOW items does not change the ordering of future change orders or reprioritization rights; both parties will need to execute subsequent change orders for additional scope.
4) DocuSign routing: recommend including a procurement contact field in the change order body so the DocuSign envelope routes to the correct PO approver at AI Health.

I've kept the edits minimal to speed review. If AI Health is comfortable with the proposed acceptance window (30 days for SOW-A criteria), I think we can circulate a DocuSign-ready change order today.

-Markus

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment: redline_comments_markus.docx (tracked changes + short commentary)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@aihealth.com, jane.sanchez@aihealth.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit reorder + scope rebalance (proposed change order)

Thanks Markus — that approach works. Jane / AI Health contracts team: we updated the redline with Markus's legal language and a short mutual action plan at the top of the change order: 

- Week of Apr 5: Legal alignment and final redline (owner: AI Health contracts / Markus)
- Apr 7: DocuSign envelope sent (owner: Redwood procurement)
- Apr 12: PO issued and first invoice scheduled for Apr 15 (owner: AI Health procurement)

Grace — can you confirm we can apply the $18k as a credit on Invoice 1 and whether procurement needs a separate 'credit' PO line? If procurement needs a PO line we will add it to the DocuSign body.

Karthik — please create/update the HubSpot deal with the new change order attachment and mark the deal stage as "Change Order: Legal review" (link below).

If AI Health is good with the acceptance language and the mutual action plan, we'll generate the DocuSign draft and share the envelope link.

Best,

Stephanie
